Granite.text: You will not be moved today, Granite. Not by argument, not by a hauler, not by the overseer. A minecart may try. Let it learn.
The stars suggest flexibility this month. Granite ignores the stars. Remain exactly where you are and wait for the world to apologize.
A friend asks you to reconsider. Consider it reconsidered and found correct the first time. Lucky stone: you. Unlucky stone: everyone who disagreed.
Someone will try to engrave your face onto a wall this month. Hold still and look stoic. You were going to anyway.
Change is coming to {fort}. You will stand in front of it with your arms folded until it gives up and goes around.
Your stubbornness pays off when the cave-in lands on everyone except you. Do not gloat. Gloat slightly, and only at dinner.
Winter freezes the river, Granite, which you take as the river finally agreeing with your general approach to life. Congratulate it.

Slate.text: Today will be fine. Tomorrow will also be fine. Slate prefers it that way. Avoid exclamation marks and anyone who uses them.
You will write something down. It will be correct. Nobody will read it. For Slate, this is the ideal outcome of any month.
A bard will sing near you. Do not react. Reacting encourages bards. Lucky color: grey. Unlucky color: also grey, but shinier.
Expect a flat month, Slate. You will thrive. Others will mistake your calm for a coma; let them check your pulse politely.
The bookkeeper needs you. Not emotionally. For counting. You are the only dwarf in {fort} who counts the socks twice.
Romance approaches in the form of a dwarf who also enjoys silence. You will sit together quietly for nine years. It will be wonderful.

Felsite.text: Nobody will notice you this month, Felsite. You are used to it. Take comfort: nobody notices the floor until it is gone.
A mason will look at you, sigh deeply, and build a wall out of you anyway. Being chosen is being chosen. Hold your head up.
Your hidden depths will finally be revealed. They turn out to be more felsite. Still, it is good to be consistent.
Felsite, you are the most common sign in the mountain, so statistically you will be stepped on. Wear sturdy boots on your feelings.
A trader will offer you nothing for yourself. Counteroffer with dignity. Then accept nothing, gracefully, like the professional you are.
This month you finally become a block. Small steps. Next year, perhaps, a table. Dream modestly and the stars will match you.

Hematite.text: Ambition burns in you like a smelter someone forgot to fuel. Fuel it, Hematite. Then forge something with a ☼ on it.
You will be promoted, or you will mention to everyone that you deserve to be. Either way, the whole dining hall will hear about it.
Your temper is iron-hard this month. Before throwing a mug, ask whether the mug deserves it. It usually does not. Throw a sock.
A rival crafts a better axe. Do not sulk. Sulk productively, at the anvil, until yours has more decorations than sense.
Hematite, the stars say rest. You hear 'rust.' You will work an extra shift out of spite, and the forges will thank you.
Red is your color. Red is also the color of the danger room floor. Wear your second-best helmet and spar with caution.

Malachite.text: You will admire your reflection in a polished gem and miss the goblin behind you. Beauty has a cost, Malachite. Usually an ear.
Envy colors your month green. Specifically, someone else's bedroom has a better cabinet. Redecorate loudly and invite them over.
A secret fondness for trees will surface. Tell no one. Especially not the woodcutter. Especially not the elves, who will be insufferable.
Wear your finest cloak to the dining hall. Nobody asked, but you look marvelous, and the plump helmets do not judge.
The stars find you fashionable this month. The stars also find you exhausting. Both things can be true, darling.
A noble will compliment your earring. Accept graciously, then immediately wonder what they want. They want your earring. Mandated, by spring.

Galena.text: Everything will be fine, Galena. Probably. Stop checking the aquifer. It is still there. It is always still there.
You sense danger. You always sense danger. This time it is only a cat. Pet the cat. Then check the walls again.
Beneath your worry lies a vein of silver. Beneath that, more worry. Mine carefully and keep the drawbridge lever within reach.
Your heart is heavy as lead this month. Avoid drinking from the well, the cistern, and especially the suspicious bucket by the hospital.
A forgotten beast is not coming. You will prepare for one anyway. When something else attacks, you will be the only dwarf ready.
Breathe deeply, Galena. Not near the miasma. Somewhere else. Somewhere with fewer corpses and much better ventilation.

Limestone.text: You will give yourself to others this month, Limestone, mostly as flux. It is a noble sacrifice. The steel will never thank you.
Everyone needs you today. The smelter, the kiln, the mason. Remember to keep one small piece of yourself uncrushed.
Say no to one request this month. Just one. Practice on the cat first. The cat will not care, which is perfect for beginners.
A helpful month ahead. You will haul, carry, fetch, and fill. Someone else will get credit for the masterpiece. Classic Limestone.
You are the quiet foundation of {fort}. Unfortunately, foundations get walked on. Also unfortunately, you secretly enjoy it.
Your many kindnesses will be repaid with a single plump helmet. Eat it slowly. Savor the recognition. It will not happen twice.

Sandstone.text: Plans crumble this month, Sandstone, but you were never very attached to them. Wander into the meeting hall and see what happens.
You meant to haul that boulder. Then you saw a butterfly. Then it was suddenly winter. The boulder understands. The overseer does not.
Relax, they say. You were already relaxed. You are so relaxed that the chief medical dwarf wants to check you for a pulse.
Something will erode this month. Probably your attention span. Possibly a wall. Look up occasionally, just in case it is the ceiling.
Take a break from your break. Then go on break. The overseer may object, but the overseer always objects. It is their hobby.
Sandstone, a cave-in will miss you by the length of a sock. You will not notice. Obliviousness is your gift. Treasure it.

Timber.text: The trees are whispering about you, Timber. They are always whispering. Carry an axe and a confident expression wherever you go.
An elf caravan arrives with opinions. You will sell them a wooden bin and watch their faces. Joy is small, and slightly cruel.
You feel restless in the stone. Take a walk outside. Look at the sky. Scream briefly. Return to the fortress refreshed.
A woodcutter will become your best friend this month. Remember: friends do not let friends fell trees near the elf border.
Timber, your roots are not in soil but in a well-made bed. Sleep longer. Grow nothing. Remain magnificently dwarvish.
Expect splinters this month, both literal and emotional. A carpenter can fix exactly one of these. Guess which one.

Moonstone.text: Strange visions approach, Moonstone. You will seize a workshop and demand shells. Nobody has shells. Begin screaming now to save time.
The moon is far above the cavern ceiling, yet you feel it. You feel everything, Moonstone. Mostly drafts from the upper ramps.
Your dreams are prophetic. Last night you dreamed of carp. Stay away from the river this month, and possibly the bathtub.
A fey mood hovers near you like a cat near an open door. Gather bones, leather, and patience. Mostly patience.
Moonstone, someone will ask what you are thinking about. Say 'stone.' It is mysterious, and also always technically true.
The stars align for an artifact. The stars do not mention it will be a ring bearing a picture of the overseer. Sorry.

Opal.text: Drama sparkles around you, Opal. Someone took your favorite chair. This is the worst thing that has ever happened. Throw something soft.
You will be the center of attention at the tavern. Unfortunately, it is because you are singing. Fortunately, the bard is worse.
A tantrum is forecast, followed by a tearful apology, followed by a second, larger tantrum. Pack a spare mug and a handkerchief.
Your talents dazzle, but your moods dazzle more. Admire the ☼ on your latest craft, then sob openly at a statue. Balance.
Opal, every color is your color. Every room is your stage. Every dwarf is your audience, whether or not they agreed to it.
This month brings applause, real or imagined. Bow anyway. The kobold watching from the shadows is clapping. Check your pockets afterward.

Obsidian.text: The magma calls to you, Obsidian. Answer it from a respectful distance. Wear something black. You already are. You always are.
Darkness suits you. Unfortunately, it also suits the cave crocodiles. Bring a torch so they can properly see you brooding.
You will write poetry about the void. The bards will steal it and add a chorus. The void, for its part, will not mind.
Obsidian, the others laugh at the party. You stand by the wall and judge the decor. The decor is beneath you. Literally, it is floor.
A memorial slab will be engraved this month. Not yours. Lean on it meaningfully anyway and stare into the middle distance.
Your sharp edge cuts deep this month. Use it to slice cheese, not friendships. Mostly cheese. Occasionally a rude goblin.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my bedroom neighbor plays the drum at all hours, and the overseer says it raises morale. My morale has never been lower. What should I do? — Sleepless by the Stockpile
advice.a: Learn the lute. Fight noise with worse noise. When the overseer complains, point out that fortress morale is now technically twice as high.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I married a dwarf for her magnificent beard, but now she wants to shave it for a festival. Is it shallow of me to object? — Bristling in the Barracks
advice.a: Yes. But festivals end and beards grow back. Love her for her other qualities, such as her excellent axe and her tolerance of you.

advice.q: Dear Urist, a cat has adopted me. I did not ask for this. Now there are eleven cats and they all follow me to the dining hall. — Furred in the Food Stockpile
advice.a: You are no longer a dwarf. You are a parade. Embrace it, and never, ever let the butcher see your entourage.

advice.q: Dear Urist, a visiting elf told me my cabinet was 'murder against the forest.' My cabinet is made of stone. Should I write to correct her? — Puzzled in Petrology
advice.a: No. Elves cannot be satisfied. If you replied, she would accuse your letter of being written on a tree.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I have been in a strange mood for three days. I keep demanding shells. We live inside a mountain. Nobody has seen a shell in years. — Moody near the Workshop
advice.a: Ask for something else. Bones are plentiful. In fact, ask quietly near the hospital and someone may offer you theirs.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my friend {citizen} keeps borrowing my socks and returning only one. I am now down to a single sock. — Unbalanced in the Upper Halls
advice.a: Sock theft is the oldest crime in dwarvenkind. Wear the survivor with pride, lock your cabinet, and take a long look at {citizen}'s feet.

advice.q: Dear Urist, everyone says I should see the sky. I went up once and it was enormous and blue and had no ceiling. I fainted into a shrub. — Agoraphobic in the Antechamber
advice.a: Perfectly normal. The sky is a design flaw. Look at it in small doses, through a fortification, while holding a mug.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my husband only drinks plump helmet wine. I brought him a mug of fine dwarven rum and he wept and called me a stranger. — Spurned at the Still
advice.a: Some dwarves are loyal to a single brew. Pour the rum into a plump helmet barrel. He will never know. Probably.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I was appointed bookkeeper and now everyone avoids me because I keep counting their things. Even their children. — Tallied in the Tavern
advice.a: Counting is a form of love. Tell them so, then count them again. Accuracy, not popularity, keeps a fortress fed.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the baron has mandated that nobody may make cups this season. I am a cup maker. I have only ever made cups. What am I now? — Mugless in the Craftshop
advice.a: You are a bowl maker with a cup maker's heart. Wait it out. Nobles forget their mandates faster than mugs break.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I keep dreaming about carp. Big carp. Hungry carp. I wake up shouting. My roommate has moved into the barracks. — Haunted by the River
advice.a: Those are not dreams, they are memories. Stay three tiles away from all water. Your roommate made the correct decision.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my toddler was carried into battle against goblins last spring and now insists on being called 'Shieldboy.' Is this a phase? — Concerned in the Creche
advice.a: No. It is a career. Get him a properly sized helmet and let him start a small militia of toddlers.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the ghost of my uncle visits every night to complain about his memorial slab. He says the engraving is 'merely competent.' — Spooked in the Sepulcher
advice.a: Commission a better engraving. Ghosts are the harshest critics in any fortress. Uncle wants a ☼ on it, and frankly he has earned one.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I have hauled for thirty years. Today I was told to carry a single pebble across the entire fort. Was my life's work worth it? — Weary on the Ramps
advice.a: Every pebble matters. Somewhere in the stockpile, that pebble is deeply grateful. Rest now. Tomorrow, another pebble.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my neighbor's kitchen smells of roast every night, but they never share. My stomach rumbles in the dark like a distant cave-in. — Hungry in Hallway Three
advice.a: Knock while holding a mug of wine. No dwarf can refuse a dwarf with a drink. It is cultural, and deeply exploitable.

advice.q: Dear Urist, a kobold stole my favorite earring right out of my cabinet. I saw him run off giggling. Should I pursue revenge? — Robbed on the Surface
advice.a: Leave a decoy earring by the gate with a cage trap underneath. Revenge, like good steel, should be tempered.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I tried to befriend an elf merchant. He gave me a wooden carving, said 'peace,' and left. I don't know how to feel. — Conflicted at the Depot
advice.a: Feel suspicious. Then sell the carving back to him next year at a markup. That is how friendship between our peoples works.

advice.q: Dear Urist, our fortress has a lovely well, but dwarves keep falling into it. Three this season. Is it the well, or is it us? — Worried at the Well
advice.a: It is both. The well is enticing and you are all curious. Build a railing. Then build a second, angrier railing.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I recently became a vampire. My friends are noticing I never eat, and that dwarves near me keep going missing. How do I tell them? — Pale in the Pantry
advice.a: Gently, and preferably from behind bars. Honesty matters, but so does a sturdy door the sheriff can lock from the outside.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my wife is a militia commander and spends all her waking hours in the danger room. I miss her terribly. — Lonely in the Lower Halls
advice.a: Visit her. Bring a training spear. Nothing says romance like being stabbed affectionately with a wooden pole.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I made a masterpiece and the fort threw a party the same day for my roommate, who made a crude sock. — Overlooked in the Workshop
advice.a: Parties are about timing, not merit. Make your next masterpiece during dinner. Loudly. With a speech prepared.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I am allergic to cats. The fort now has {cats} of them and I sneeze into my beard from dawn until dusk. — Sniffling in {fort}
advice.a: Grow your beard longer and denser. Eventually it becomes a natural filter. Many great dwarves have breathed exclusively through their beards.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the trade caravan left and took my heart with it. Also my lucky hammer, which I traded for a sack of nuts. — Regretful near the Gate
advice.a: Hearts return with the next caravan. Hammers do not. Next year, trade your nuts and keep your tools.

advice.q: Dear Urist, a forgotten beast made of salt has been watching my cavern farm for a week. It seems lonely. Should I invite it to dinner? — Curious in the Caverns
advice.a: Absolutely not. It will season everything, including you. Seal the cavern and send it a polite note through a fortification.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the new migrants were all assigned to my bedroom. There are four of them now. One of them is a goat. — Crowded in the Dormitory
advice.a: Ask the manager for a bedroom. Meanwhile, the goat is likely the best roommate of the bunch. Befriend the goat.

advice.q: Dear Urist, during a tantrum I threw a mug at the mayor. Now I am famous throughout the fortress. Is this a good career move? — Notorious in the Noble Wing
advice.a: Fame through mug-throwing is fleeting. Write a book about it for the library. Fame through literature is also fleeting, but quieter.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the overseer dug a channel straight through my bedroom. There is now a waterfall where my bed used to be. — Damp in Dormitory Six
advice.a: Congratulations, you now live in a scenic suite. Charge admission. Nobles pay handsomely to sit near waterfalls.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my son wants to be a bard. His father was a miner, as was his father before him. Where did I go wrong? — Despairing in the Deep
advice.a: You fed him plump helmets and told him stories. That is how bards happen. Encourage him to sing exclusively about mining.

advice.q: Dear Urist, we ran out of booze and I have been drinking only water for a week. Everyone is grumpy. I am the grumpiest. — Parched in the Pantry
advice.a: Water is a crime against dwarvenkind. Bribe the brewer with socks, plant more plump helmets, and sing no songs until the barrels are full.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I may be the only dwarf in the mountain who likes elves. I keep it a secret. Is something deeply wrong with me? — Leafy at Heart
advice.a: Nothing is wrong, merely unfashionable. Keep the secret. Never mention trees in the dining hall, and never mention elves near the axe rack.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I raised my dog from a puppy. Now he follows the hunter everywhere and ignores me completely. — Abandoned in the Kennel
advice.a: Dogs love whoever smells of meat. Carry a sausage in your pocket. It is not true love, but it is close enough for dwarves.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I fell into a pit while hauling and nobody in the fort noticed I was gone for three whole days. Should I be offended? — Forgotten Below
advice.a: Yes, but also proud. Three days alone in a pit is a true test of dwarven fortitude. Climb out and demand a party.

advice.q: Dear Urist, a necromancer moved into the tower next door. He seems polite, but all his pets are skeletons and they stare at me. — Rattled in the Annex
advice.a: Good neighbors are hard to find. Stay cordial, keep the drawbridge lever close, and never, ever lend him a shovel.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I went to the hospital with a broken leg. The doctor put a cast on my other leg, then on my arm. — Limping in the Hospital
advice.a: Medical science is still developing. Walk on your hands until he gets it right. It builds excellent upper body strength.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I am afraid of magma. Everyone at the forges says I am being silly and laughs at me. Am I silly? — Sweating near the Forges
advice.a: No. Magma is extremely dangerous, and anyone who says otherwise has not met magma yet. Stay afraid. Stay alive. Stay three tiles away.

advice.q: Dear Urist, I gave my axe a name and now I feel too attached to actually use it. The goblins arrive next week. — Sentimental in the Armory
advice.a: Name a second axe for chopping and keep the first for emotional support. Most champions carry two for exactly this reason.

advice.q: Dear Urist, the meeting hall is always full of loud, happy dwarves. I want to be loud and happy too, but I am shy. — Quiet in the Corner
advice.a: Start small. Raise your mug. Next week, raise it higher. By winter you will be dancing on a table and regretting nothing.

advice.q: Dear Urist, my oldest friend {promoted} got a fancy new title and now expects me to knock before entering the dining hall. — Demoted by Association
advice.a: Titles go to the head faster than wine. Knock, but knock with a rhythm that says you remember the time they fell in the latrine.

recipes.title: Plump Helmet Surprise
ingredients: a pinch of ground plump helmet
recipes.method: Chop the plump helmets. Add the other plump helmet. Season with plump helmet. Serve to the dining hall, who will be surprised, mostly that it is plump helmets again.

recipes.title: Carp Revenge Stew
recipes.method: Catch the carp before it catches you. Bandage the fisherdwarf. Boil the carp until it stops looking smug. Eat with confidence and keep a shield within reach.

recipes.title: Elven Disappointment Salad
recipes.method: Arrange the leaves sadly. Place the twig on top. Serve to an elf diplomat, who will call it barbaric anyway. Eat it yourself, then wash it down with wine.

recipes.title: Magma-Seared Steak
recipes.method: Hold the steak over the magma for half a heartbeat. It is done. So are the tongs. Eat quickly, before the dining hall catches fire and the overseer notices.

recipes.title: Dwarven Syrup Pancakes
recipes.method: Heat the slab near the forge. Pour batter. Flip with a battleaxe. Drown in syrup until the pancake becomes structurally unsound. Serve to children carried home from battle.

recipes.title: Sock Soup
recipes.method: Boil the sock until the water turns a color not found in nature. Add optimism. Serve to anyone who stole your other sock. Watch them eat it. Feel justice.

recipes.title: Goblin-Siege Ration Bar
recipes.method: Press everything into a brick. Bake until it can deflect an arrow. Distribute to the militia, who may eat it or use it as a shield. Both are recommended.

recipes.title: Tantrum Toast
recipes.method: Toast the bread. Burn it. Scream. Throw the mug. Pick up the mug. Apologize to the mug. Butter the toast anyway. Eat it while staring furiously at the kitchen wall.

recipes.title: Bookkeeper's Accurate Pie
recipes.method: Count the pods. Count them again. Write down the number. Bake. Cut into slices of precisely equal size, then recount. Serve only once everyone's portion has been entered into the books.

recipes.title: Catch-of-the-Day Vermin Pie
recipes.method: Collect the offerings the cats left on your bed. Do not ask what they are. Wrap in pastry, bake thoroughly, and call it a regional specialty when guests inquire.

recipes.title: Rock Nut Brittle
recipes.method: Boil the syrup, pour over the nuts, and let it set into something geologically significant. Break it with a hammer. Eat carefully. The mason may want to use leftovers for walls.

recipes.title: Quarry Bush Leaf Wrap
recipes.method: Lay out a leaf. Place the fish on it. Add cheese. Roll it up like a tiny scroll. Hand it to a dwarf in the library and say it contains wisdom. It contains fish.

recipes.title: Sweet Pod Jam
recipes.method: Mash the pods. Add sugar. Stir for three days while the stirrer questions their life choices. Pour into jars. Spread on anything that does not move, and some things that do.

recipes.title: Strange Mood Soufflé
recipes.method: Seize the kitchen. Allow no one inside. Mutter. Whisk the eggs while staring at the ceiling. Demand a shell. When the soufflé rises it will bear a ☼ and a title nobody can pronounce.

recipes.title: Fey Workshop Fondue
recipes.method: Melt the cheese in a workshop nobody else may enter. Dip things into it for several days. Emerge holding a legendary fondue fork engraved with images of cheese. Faint. Your skills have improved.

recipes.title: Trade Depot Leftovers
recipes.method: Open the mystery barrel. If it hisses, close the barrel. If it does not hiss, stir it into the bucket. Serve warm and tell everyone it is a foreign delicacy. Technically, it is.

recipes.title: Noble's Mandated Meringue
recipes.method: Beat the whites until stiff, as the mandate requires. Decorate with gold because the baron insists. Present it on a gem-studded plate. The baron will take one bite and ask for plump helmets.

recipes.title: Cave Spider Silk Noodles
recipes.method: Roll the dough thin. Tie each noodle shut with silk so it cannot escape. Boil. Remove the silk before serving, unless you are cooking for a goblin, in which case leave it in.

recipes.title: Bard's Lament Dumplings
recipes.method: Fold the meat into the dough while the bard sings about lost loves. The dumplings will absorb the melancholy and taste faintly of regret. Pairs well with ale and avoiding eye contact.

recipes.title: Militia Morning Porridge
recipes.method: Boil the grain until it surrenders. Stand at attention while eating. Finish in under one minute or repeat the danger room. Second helpings are earned only by surviving the first.

recipes.title: Kobold-Proof Cake
recipes.method: Bake the cake. Frost it lavishly. Place it in the cage on the pressure plate. Wait for a giggle in the dark. Enjoy the cake and your new kobold, in that order.

recipes.title: The Overseer's Choice
ingredients: whatever is in the nearest stockpile
recipes.method: The overseer designates a meal. The cook interprets it freely. Nobody knows what was intended. Eat it with the same blind faith you bring to every other order from above.

recipes.title: Barrel-Bottom Wine Gravy
ingredients: the last inch of a wine barrel
recipes.method: Scrape the barrel. Mourn briefly. Thicken with flour and drippings. Pour over anything. Note: if the fortress has reached the bottom of the barrel, the gravy is the least of your problems.

recipes.title: Turkey Egg Omelette Supreme
recipes.method: Collect the eggs quickly while the turkey is distracted. Whisk with cheese. Add mushroom. Fry. Eat the omelette before the turkey files a complaint with the sheriff.

recipes.title: Pump-Operator Pickles
recipes.method: Fill the jar using the pump stack, because carrying water is beneath us. The operator will be exhausted and thirsty. Do not give them the brine. They will try. Stop them.

recipes.title: Suspiciously Lively Bone Broth
ingredients: a lid with a weight on it
recipes.method: Simmer the bones for hours. If the bones climb out of the pot, you have accidentally bought them from a necromancer. Put the lid back and call the militia.

riddles.q: Why did the dwarf bring a ladder to the tavern?
riddles.a: He heard the drinks were on the house.

riddles.q: What do you call a carp that has never attacked a dwarf?
riddles.a: Not hungry yet.

riddles.q: Why don't elves play cards in the fortress?
riddles.a: The cards are made from trees, so they hold a funeral every time someone shuffles.

riddles.q: I am poured but never drunk, I flow but never run, I make dwarves rich and goblins crispy. What am I?
riddles.a: Magma.

riddles.q: How many dwarves does it take to change a torch?
riddles.a: One to change it, eleven to throw a party, and one to throw a tantrum about not being invited.

riddles.q: What goes into the stockpile in pairs but always comes out alone?
riddles.a: Socks.

riddles.q: Why did the hauler cross the fortress?
riddles.a: To pick up a single pebble on the other side. Then he went back for its friend.

riddles.q: What do you call a dwarf who has just seen the sky for the first time?
riddles.a: Upset.

riddles.q: Why did the noble mandate golden toothpicks?
riddles.a: Because silver ones would be ridiculous.

riddles.q: What has four legs, purrs, and multiplies whenever you look away?
riddles.a: A cat. Look away for one season and count again.

riddles.q: What is a goblin's favorite game?
riddles.a: Hide and siege.

riddles.q: Why did the kobold steal the calendar?
riddles.a: He wanted to take a month off.

riddles.q: What room has no walls, no floor, and no way out?
riddles.a: The bedroom the overseer designated over the chasm.

riddles.q: What gets wetter the more it works?
riddles.a: The pump operator.

riddles.q: Why don't dwarves whisper secrets in the library?
riddles.a: The walls are engraved, and the engravings are always watching.

riddles.q: What do you call a dwarf in a strange mood with no materials?
riddles.a: A screaming problem with a workshop.

riddles.q: What breaks when dropped, holds wine, and has been thrown at every mayor in history?
riddles.a: A mug.

riddles.q: Why was the bookkeeper always so calm?
riddles.a: He could always count on something.

riddles.q: Why did the vampire make such a good bookkeeper?
riddles.a: He never slept and he was very interested in everyone's blood type.

riddles.q: What has a mouth but never eats, yet swallows any dwarf who leans too far?
riddles.a: The well.

riddles.q: What do you call a dwarf who loves trees?
riddles.a: Under investigation.

riddles.q: What is lighter than a feather, yet no dwarf can hold it for very long?
riddles.a: Their temper.

riddles.q: Why are dwarven babies so brave in battle?
riddles.a: Nobody asked them first.

riddles.q: What do a werebeast and a full moon have in common?
riddles.a: Terrible timing.

riddles.q: What runs on rails, carries ore, and screams?
riddles.a: A minecart. Well, the dwarf standing in front of it screams.

riddles.q: What do you call a miner who keeps digging after striking adamantine?
riddles.a: Lucky. Then extremely unlucky.

riddles.q: Where do dwarves keep their best jokes?
riddles.a: In the cellar. They need to age in a barrel first.

riddles.q: Why did the bard sing to the stone wall?
riddles.a: It was the only audience that couldn't leave.

riddles.q: What are the three things a dwarf says upon breaching the caverns?
riddles.a: 'Strike the earth!' Then, 'What is that?' Then, 'Run.'

riddles.q: Why do dwarves never get lost underground?
riddles.a: Every corridor eventually leads to a tavern.

riddles.q: What do you call a cave-in during supper?
riddles.a: Dinner and a show.

riddles.q: Why did the cheesemaker refuse to join the militia?
riddles.a: He was afraid he would curdle under pressure.

riddles.q: What weighs a ton, never complains, and gets carved into a statue of the mayor anyway?
riddles.a: A boulder of {stone}, which deserved better.

riddles.q: What fires a thousand bolts and still never hits the goblin?
riddles.a: A newly recruited marksdwarf.

riddles.q: Why was the forgotten beast so sad?
riddles.a: Nobody remembered its birthday. Or its name. Or that it existed.

riddles.q: What do you call the dwarf who dug into the aquifer?
riddles.a: Everyone's least favorite dwarf, and extremely damp.

riddles.q: What is the one thing every fortress does eventually, and every dwarf agrees is fun?
riddles.a: Losing.

riddles.q: What arrives at the depot every spring, is mostly leaves, and judges your furniture?
riddles.a: The elven caravan.

riddles.q: What happens when you forget to bury a dwarf?
riddles.a: He comes back to remind you, usually at night, usually upset about his socks.

riddles.q: What happens when a fortress has two cats and one season of neglect?
riddles.a: A catsplosion. Nobody survives with their furniture unscratched.

riddles.q: Why did the ghost keep lying in the hospital bed?
riddles.a: He heard the doctor still hadn't finished his checkup.

riddles.q: Which noble never has trouble getting dwarves to listen?
riddles.a: The hammerer. Everyone pays very close attention.

riddles.q: If every dwarf in the mountain is named Urist, how do you call one to dinner?
riddles.a: You don't. You ring the bell and all of them come.
